subject: zoology
question_text: What is the strongest cartilage? In which regions of the human body do you find it?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.52, VSAQ 81). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The strongest cartilage
steps.why: Strength in cartilage comes from collagen, so naming the thick fibre bundles explains the answer instead of only stating it.
common_mistakes: Naming hyaline cartilage. Hyaline is the weakest and the commonest.
Naming elastic cartilage. Elastic cartilage is springy, not the strongest.
steps.memory_tip: Fibrous means fibres, and fibres mean strength. Hyaline is the weakest, elastic is the springy one.
steps.margin_note: Two words are the mark — fibrous cartilage. Add one line on why.
lines: Fibrous cartilage is the strongest cartilage.
Its matrix holds thick bundles of collagen
fibres, and those give it the strength.

steps.label: Where it is found
steps.why: Both places carry heavy pressure all day, which is why the strongest cartilage is placed there.
common_mistakes: Giving the pinna or the epiglottis. Those are elastic cartilage.
steps.memory_tip: Both places take the body's weight: the discs of the spine and the joint of the hip bones.
steps.margin_note: Two places carry this mark. Name both.
lines: It is found in the intervertebral discs
